1.note: Literally 'you have no dispute or words', i.e., no legitimate claim; the source paraphrased is 4 Maccabees / Yosippon rather than 2 Macc 3 verbatim.

2.note: Probably Philo's De monarchia (now part of De specialibus legibus I); identification likely but not certain.

3.note: Probably Philo's De victimis (De specialibus legibus I); the passage on the tamid as thanksgiving for all mankind fits Spec. 1.168–169.

4.note: Eusebius, Praeparatio evangelica 8.2 contains Aristeas material; the Against Apion passage (2.196–197) is cited by Eusebius elsewhere (8.8). The reference is kept as given.

5.note: The sense of התעלם is unclear: it may mean Abravanel 'ignored' these prayers, or (less likely) 'dealt at length' with them. The Mishnah cited is m. Avot 4:22.

6.note: בא"ה is taken as באומות העולם, 'among the nations'. The Latin source of the Seneca saying has not been verified.

7.note: An Aramaic play on b. Pesahim 25b ('who says your blood is redder'): the blood of all of them is 'ours', equally red and precious.
